import bpy, math
bpy.data.objects.remove(bpy.data.objects["Cube"], do_unlink=True)

def mat(name, col, metal=0.0, rough=0.5):
    m = bpy.data.materials.new(name); m.use_nodes = True
    b = next(n for n in m.node_tree.nodes if n.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED")
    b.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = col
    b.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = metal
    b.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = rough
    m.diffuse_color = col
    return m

blue = bpy.data.materials.get("Blue") or mat("Blue", (0,0.1,1,1))
tire = mat("Tire", (0.03,0.03,0.03,1), rough=0.8)
plat = mat("Platform", (0.8,0.8,0.82,1), metal=0.3, rough=0.25)

def finish(o, name, m):
    o.name = name; o.data.materials.append(m)

# Platform: top surface at z=0.2
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=4, depth=0.2, vertices=64, location=(0,0,0.1))
finish(bpy.context.object, "Platform", plat)

# Body
bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1, location=(0,0,0.95))
body = bpy.context.object; body.scale = (2.4,1.2,0.5)
finish(body, "Rover_Body", blue)

# Wheels
for i,(x,y) in enumerate([(0.9,0.85),(-0.9,0.85),(0.9,-0.85),(-0.9,-0.85)]):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(radius=0.5, depth=0.3, vertices=32,
        location=(x,y,0.7), rotation=(math.radians(90),0,0))
    finish(bpy.context.object, f"Rover_Wheel_{i+1}", tire)
print([o.name for o in bpy.data.objects])
